topic: 5 things you need to know: Anthropic files to go public
post:
The company behind Claude just filed to go public. 📈
Here are 5 things you need to know about Anthropic's IPO filing.

1️⃣ It's official
Anthropic filed its S-1 with the SEC on October 26. It plans to list on Nasdaq under the ticker "ANT". The share price and number of shares aren't set yet.

2️⃣ Big revenue
Per reporting on the filing, revenue in the first half of 2026 was about $16.3 billion.

3️⃣ Bigger losses
The filing shows a net loss of about $80.7 billion for the same period, mostly from accounting charges.

4️⃣ Huge compute bills
Anthropic has agreed to spend up to $120.5 billion on compute through 2029, including about $3.1 billion a month to SpaceX for NVIDIA-powered compute once it's all delivered.

5️⃣ Honest risks
It flags tension with the Trump administration and the Department of Defense as a possible cause of material revenue loss, and warns models could develop capabilities it doesn't anticipate.

Why it matters:
An IPO filing is the most detailed public look yet at what it costs to build frontier AI. The money is enormous on both sides. 🔍

Practical takeaway:
If your team relies on an AI vendor, read their public filings and risk sections. They tell you more than any demo. 📄
